newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen forces make more gains against royalists.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen forces make more gains against royalists.

text.p: Forces under Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen regained a foothold in the royalist-controlled border town of Poipet without firing a shot after rival forces agreed to share power, royalist sources said here on Wednesday.
It was further evidence of Hun Sen's sweep of the countryside since ousting First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh in the capital Phnom Penh earlier this month after two days of bloodshed.

Delegates from Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) led by Colonel Mai Sang Hin reached a pact with the commander of the royalist-aligned 12th Division, Lay Vireak, after three hours of talks, the sources told Reuters.
Their power-sharing deal will come into effect on Thursday and some of the 600 royalist soldiers in Poipet said they were relieved they would not have to fight their former comrades.
"I am glad we have reached a peaceful settlement instead of fighting," Captain Chhorn Varanridh, an officer with royalist forces based here told Reuters.
"From tomorrow, the CPP will resume joint operations in all sections of the town," an immigration official affiliated to Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party said.

Fighting erupted between forces loyal to the two prime ministers in Phnom Penh on July 5. Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh the following day as his forces pushed Ranariddh's men from the city and its outskirts.
The two formed an uneasy coalition government after FUNCINPEC narrowly won U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993. That relationship had been unravelling long before Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh.

Within days of the prince's ouster, clashes erupted in northern Cambodia, near the tourist town of Siem Reap and the Angkor Wat temple complex, but better-equipped forces under Hun Sen pushed the royalists back into northern jungles within a few days.

In the trade town of Poipet and elsewhere, royalist forces braced for battle with Hun Sen's men but the troops here agreed to a power-sharing deal after CPP troops began infiltrating into the area, the royalist sources said.
While his forces winning victories on the battlefield, Hun Sen has been pushing ahead with moves to legitimise his new government in Phnom Penh.
He said the CPP-FUNCINPEC coalition would remain in place and elections would be held as planned next May.

On Wednesday, Foreign Minister Ung Huot, a respected senior member of Ranariddh's party, said he was willing to take over the prince's job as first prime minister. Political anlaysts in Phnom Penh said the move would be welcomed in the region and improve the image of Hun Sen's government.
But in Poipet dozens of opposition sympathisers said they were shocked to hear about the local-level deal and that they were preparing to flee the town.

"We are very scared of Hun Sen, and now his soldiers will come here we have to find a way out from this town as soon as possible," said a member of the Khmer Nation Party, a royalist ally led by former finance minister Sam Rainsy.
A diplomatic source in Phnom Penh said up to 40 Cambodians may have been killed for political reasons since Ranariddh's ouster.
